transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-29
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Noah Patel (Redwood Product), Priya Anand (CTO - Celestial Kiosk), Marco Ruiz (Cloud Eng), Sophie Tan (PM)

Auto-summary (auto): quick sync on marketplace listing and private deployment tradeoffs, agreed to next steps and benchmarks.

[00:00] Maya Chen: ok everybody can hear me? hi Priya, Marco, Sophie, thanks for making time.
[00:10] Priya Anand: yes, hearing you Maya, thanks.
[00:12] Marco Ruiz: good to be here. we have a hard stop at 17:00 local so around 52 minutes.
[00:18] Maya Chen: perfect. quick agenda — packaging for marketplace listing, private deploy constraints (vpc/kms, air-gap), quantization/latency/cost tradeoffs, and pilot plan. Liam will take the deep technical parts.
[00:30] Liam Ortiz: hey all, yeah I'll run through serving/runtime notes then jump into quantization bench plan.
[00:38] Sophie Tan: also want to confirm acceptance criteria from product side — what counts as success for the pilot.

[02:05] Liam Ortiz: first, packaging — marketplace wants a container image plus a listing manifest, and for hybrid we provide an adapter helm chart. note: the listing checklist that Maya has includes required telemetry hooks, health endpoints, and minimal resource defs.
[02:30] Maya Chen: i'll post the checklist after the call — it's the same template we used for other partners but we'll call out the KMS options for you.
[03:03] Marco Ruiz: on KMS, our security team prefers customer-managed keys (HSM) or a bring-your-own-kms flow. we are regulated so we need audit logs that show key usage.
[03:25] Noah Patel: we support both. in Private we can wire to your KMS via an operator that uses the native cloud KMS API or through a vault/HSM connector for on-prem. audit logs are emitted to our control plane with configurable retention on Dedicated/Private.
[03:50] Priya Anand: retention — we need 7 years for certain logs, is that possible?
[04:00] Liam Ortiz: 7 years is unusual but our enterprise retention addon can be configured for longer storage; costs apply. we'll surface the retention SLA and costs in the runbook.

[05:10] Sophie Tan: about latency — we tested a hosted API earlier and saw jitter with our spike traffic. curious how Dedicated vs Private will behave and what's realistic for p95.
[05:35] Liam Ortiz: good question. with Dedicated reserved GPU pools you get predictable throughput and lower jitter. for on-prem it depends on your infra (network and HPA). typical p95 for gen-2 models on Dedicated is 120–250ms depending on sequence length and batching. if you enable prefix KV cache and smart batching we can push p95 down but it's workload dependent.
[06:02] Marco Ruiz: sequence lengths are often short for us (customer support prompts, ~60 tokens), we care more about tail latency. we also need to cap cost.
[06:20] Liam Ortiz: for short sequences caching helps; also lower-precision quantization (int8) gives big cost wins but watch for accuracy drift. we'll run a quantization eval on a small prompt set.

[08:00] Maya Chen: can we talk through the pilot? ideal pilot: 2-week on-prem lab with representative traffic, our SE runs bench and then we do a canary roll on Dedicated. does that align?
[08:18] Priya Anand: yes but compliance wants to see the KMS and network diagram before anything.
[08:26] Maya Chen: understood. we'll provide a network runbook and KMS integration notes.

[09:40] Liam Ortiz: demoing a bit — (audio skippable) — when we onboard we provide a helm chart and a small operator that sets up the adapter. attestation and cert rotation are supported. for air-gapped we hand over a tarball + offline installer.
[10:05] Marco Ruiz: offline installer — what's the upgrade flow for that?
[10:12] Liam Ortiz: upgrades are via signed bundle; we can guide your SREs on how to validate and apply. it's a manual roll by default but we can automate via your internal pipeline.

[12:00] Sophie Tan: marketplace listing question — will listing require us to expose any endpoints externally? we want to keep everything private for now.
[12:20] Maya Chen: no, listing is metadata in the cloud marketplace registry. runtime can remain private. the listing simply makes your product discoverable and provides install artifacts (helm, container images) that you control.
[12:38] Priya Anand: ok good. any special compliance language in the listing?
[12:45] Maya Chen: we have a standard compliance block; if you need custom text we can work with legal.

[14:20] Liam Ortiz: quantization tradeoffs — int8 reduces memory and doubles batch capacity on some GPUs, but QAT (quant aware training) is better for quality. post-training static quantization is fastest to experiment with. we can run an ablation: int8 static vs int8 QAT vs fp16.
[14:45] Marco Ruiz: what's the usual accuracy loss?
[14:50] Liam Ortiz: depends on model; for many open Llama-like models it's sub 1–2% on common NLU tasks for static int8, but in hallucination-sensitive prompts you might see edge cases. that's why we tie quantization to evals.

[17:00] Priya Anand: cost model — can you estimate unit costs for our 10k monthly queries?
[17:18] Noah Patel: we'll need your token distribution and concurrency. rough guess: on Hosted with mixed model likely X, Dedicated maybe 40–60% cheaper depending on utilization. we'll produce a spreadsheet.
[17:37] Marco Ruiz: i'll share the traffic profile after the call.

[19:30] Sophie Tan: regarding rollouts — we want canary traffic routing and automatic fallback to hosted if Dedicated fails. is that supported?
[19:45] Liam Ortiz: yes, smart routing policies allow region/model tier fallback. route rules can be time-based or error-based, with circuit breakers. for your use case we can do a 10% canary with auto rollback on latency/error thresholds.

[22:55] Priya Anand: audit — we need to ensure any PII doesn't leave our VPC. how do you handle logs/kv cache?
[23:10] Liam Ortiz: KV cache and prefix caches are configurable; we can disable persistent KV for PII flows and only use in-memory caches. log redaction is supported and you can route logs to your own syslog/Kafka via our connectors.
[23:35] Marco Ruiz: and encryption at rest for model artifacts?
[23:40] Noah Patel: yes, artifacts in Private use customer KMS and can be encrypted with your keys. for Dedicated we support envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys or customer keys.

[26:00] Maya Chen: small note on telemetry — marketplace listing requires basic telemetry (health, version). advanced telemetry (token-level breakdowns) is an add-on.
[26:20] Sophie Tan: price for telemetry add-on?
[26:25] Maya Chen: we'll list in the pricing doc; it's usage-tiered.

[29:10] Liam Ortiz: now onto benchmarks — plan: 1) collect your trace 2) run perf on Dedicated and on Private lab 3) run quantization variants 4) produce a p95/p99 and cost-per-1M tokens table. we'll need representative prompts and a seed set of 200–500 eval prompts.
[29:40] Marco Ruiz: we can provide that. also want to test cold-start behavior and KV cache warmup.
[29:50] Liam Ortiz: yep include cold start scenarios. we'll instrument warmup traces and show the delta.

[32:05] Priya Anand: any concerns about model licensing? we're wanting to use an open model but may need a fine-tuned variant. how are weights handled?
[32:20] Noah Patel: we onboard models after license review. for fine-tuning you can bring your weights; deployments can host the fine-tuned weights in Private with your KMS encryption. we can also help with version pinning and rollout policies.

[35:00] Sophie Tan: SSO/SSO mapping — our identity is SAML. do you support SAML for the console and audit access?
[35:10] Maya Chen: yes SAML/SSO supported, RBAC mapping included. for Private we can integrate with your IdP on-prem.

[36:30] Marco Ruiz: Egress billing — if we keep data in our VPC but connect to Redwood control plane, any egress charges we should expect?
[36:45] Noah Patel: minimal—control plane traffic is small. large model artifacts or telemetry export to Redwood's cloud may incur egress; we'll annotate the runbook with expected egress patterns and cost approximations.

[39:10] Liam Ortiz: a note on observability — we'll provide dashboards for per-route latency, token breakdown, and model regressions. rollouts are tied to eval results so you can gate based on quality regressions.
[39:30] Priya Anand: want regression alerts to hit our PagerDuty. possible?
[39:36] Liam Ortiz: yes, PagerDuty integration available.

[42:00] Sophie Tan: any red flags we're missing?
[42:10] Maya Chen: only the usual: need your sample traffic, confirm KMS mode, and specify retention. once we have that, Redwood SE will run the lab and share results.

[44:20] Marco Ruiz: timeline check — after we share the trace this week, when can lab happen?
[44:28] Liam Ortiz: earliest next week but realistically two weeks for full quantization eval; pilot kickoffs target week of 2026-08-10.

[47:00] Priya Anand: legal/procurement — can you share a preliminary pricing sheet and marketplace terms?
[47:10] Maya Chen: yes i'll add to next steps.

[49:50] Sophie Tan: one last: competitor question — other vendors tied us to their hosted only path; we like Redwood's private option. any differences we should watch for compared to CloudGenius?
[50:05] Liam Ortiz: main diffs are runtime-level batching/caching knobs and unified API across hosted/dedicated/private — plus observability tied to evals. CloudGenius tends to have less unified tooling for onprem.

[51:10] Maya Chen: ok i'll recap next steps in email and attach checklist + doc links. thanks everyone; we'll follow up with the runbook and schedule.
[51:28] Priya Anand: thanks everyone.
[51:30] Marco Ruiz: thanks, bye.

Questions (auto): who owns KMS integration (Marco/Redwood), what sample traffic format, target pilot dates.
